answer: At birth each identity is entrusted with a different bulky archive — one keeps cedar ship logs, another sable-trade ledgers — and pay comes only for tending that relic: answering unpredictable queries about its contents and folding in daily updates. Queries are bound to that archive, so a copied answer is worthless, and each clone drags a full, distinct archive it must store, read and update in real time. One honest keeper pays the cost once; a sybil farmer pays it fifty times over, while earnings stay flat per archive, making the fleet a burden, not a multiplier.
